title: deployable rbacv2 hook: kms verifier and audit compactifier
author: Priya Menon
description:
Context: Customers operating in regulated jurisdictions require deterministic enforcement of RBAC v2 policy decisions at the request ingress point, an independent KMS key provenance check, and compact audit envelopes to reduce downstream storage costs. This PR introduces a small, deployable 'policy hook' sidecar + library that performs an admission-time RBAC v2 assertion check, validates KMS key residency/attestation for keys referenced by the request, and emits a compact, canonicalized audit record that preserves necessary provenance while trimming verbose payloads. Motivation: avoid latency spikes from monolithic policy paths, provide a reusable hook for Dedicated/Private installs, and centralize compliance transforms for audit ingestion.

What this PR changes (high level):
- Add services/policy-hook/ - a lightweight Go service that can be run as a sidecar or as an internal lower-latency process. It exposes a small gRPC API for policy evaluation and a REST shim for compatibility with existing ingress proxies.
- Add pkg/kms/verifier/ - KMS attestation client that fetches and validates key residency claims and signature provenance from configured KMS providers. Supports multi-provider fallback and configurable timeouts.
- Add pkg/audit/compactifier/ - transforms full audit JSON into a deterministic compact envelope (HMAC'd index, minimal claim set, compressed tokenized blobs) suitable for long-term storage and fast diffs.
- Wire the hook into the ingress routing table (routes/ingress/annotations and a small config entry in config/policy-hook.yaml), and add canary rollout flags for Dedicated clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear (ENG-2048)
- [x] Unit tests for verifier and compactifier
- [x] Integration test that runs the hook against a local KMS emulator
- [x] Backwards-compatible REST shim for existing proxies
- [x] Feature-flagged rollout path (canary -> full)

Testing performed:
- Unit test suite: pkg/kms/verifier (98% coverage on core logic), pkg/audit/compactifier (deterministic serialization tests)
- Local integration: ran hook against kms-emulator v0.9 and sample ingress payloads; verified audit envelopes are deterministic and HMAC signatures validate with stored keys
- Load smoke: simulated 200 simultaneous small requests; median added latency ~3ms, p99 ~18ms (within SLO)
- End-to-end canary on staging cluster for 48 hours; no errors and audit ingestion volume reduced by ~6.8% due to compactification and dedupe fingerprinting.

Rollback plan:
- Feature is behind config/policy_hook.enabled and a per-cluster canary annotation. To roll back: flip config/policy_hook.enabled=false and restart ingress pods; compactifier is non-blocking for reads.
- If KMS provider errors spike, the hook falls back to a 'defer-to-main' mode exposed by policy_hook.failure_mode=passthrough in config.

Related and notes:
- Inspired by prior work in PRs that added residency proof publishers; this focuses on deployable/edge enforceability, not policy graph migration.
- Linear ENG-2048 contains architecture sketches and telemetry expectations.

Reasoning on security decisions:
- KMS verifier uses signed claims from provider endpoints and verifies both origin and residency timestamp to avoid replayed attestations. There is a small cache with TTL to reduce KMS call volume; cache respects on-demand invalidation hooks for key rotation.
- Compactifier intentionally drops request body contents unless they are marked as 'evidence' in the policy evaluation result. This reduces risk surface in long-lived audit storage while preserving chain-of-custody hashes.
